questions.q: Before loading any real data, why did the Meridian plan start with exporting the org's current data?
options: Exports are required by Salesforce before any Data Loader job can run
It creates a safety net to recover from if the load goes wrong
Exported data automatically becomes the External ID field
It disables validation rules during the import
questions.explain: Backing up current data before a large load is a Chapter 2 habit — it protects the org if something in the migration goes badly.

questions.q: Why was the duplicate rule for "Trailhead Gear Co" set to Allow + Report instead of Block?
options: It let the import complete while flagging likely matches for a human to review afterward, rather than halting the migration
Block is not a valid action for Account duplicate rules
Allow + Report runs faster than Block during bulk imports
Report-only rules cannot use fuzzy matching
questions.explain: For a one-time migration with known regional overlap, flagging likely duplicates for review (without blocking the load) is usually the more practical choice than stopping the import outright.

questions.q: Why did the first batch of Contacts fail with INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY?
options: The Contacts file was missing a required field
The Contact object does not support bulk loading
A validation rule blocked every Contact record
Accounts and Contacts were submitted in the same batch, so Contacts referenced Account Ids that didn't exist yet
questions.explain: Parent records (Accounts) need to be loaded and confirmed before child records (Contacts) that reference them — loading them together broke the lookup.

questions.q: What caused the smaller wave of DUPLICATE_VALUE errors during the migration?
options: A Duplicate Rule configured with the Block action
The Legacy_Account_ID__c field was not marked as required
Two different regions had coincidentally reused the same legacy spreadsheet row ID
A formula field referenced itself
questions.explain: DUPLICATE_VALUE is a hard Unique-field constraint. Here it exposed that two regions' spreadsheets happened to reuse the same row number as their own 'unique' ID, requiring manual correction.

questions.q: Why does the case study connect clean data directly to the next course in the path, Reports & Dashboards?
options: Reports and dashboards cannot be built until every Duplicate Record Set is deleted
A report grouped on messy or duplicated data would be misleading in the same ways described earlier in the course, so clean data is a prerequisite for trustworthy reporting
The next course requires re-importing all data using SOQL instead of Data Loader
Reports & Dashboards is unrelated to data management and simply follows it in course order
questions.explain: A grouped or filtered report inherits whatever data quality problems exist underneath it — the cleanup in this lesson is what makes the upcoming reporting work meaningful.
